title: How Much a Drug Changes a Step

scenes.tts: A drug that fills nine in ten of its targets looks nearly done. Is it?
scenes.visual: Title fades. A field of 100 transporter dots, 90 of them filled. The question appears beside it.
scenes.narration: A drug that fills nine in ten of its targets looks nearly done. Is it?

scenes.tts: Take paroxetine. It blocks the transporter that clears serotonin.
scenes.visual: A serotonin synapse; transporters in the terminal membrane pull serotonin back in. A paroxetine icon labelled reuptake blocker.
scenes.narration: Take paroxetine. It blocks the transporter that clears serotonin.

scenes.tts: Picture the transporters as a field of dots. As the drug's concentration rises, the dots fill.
scenes.visual: The dot field fills as a concentration slider moves right. Beside it, an occupancy curve draws on a log axis: concentration along the bottom, share filled up the side.
scenes.narration: Picture the transporters as a field of dots. As the drug's concentration rises, the dots fill.

scenes.tts: Half fill at a very low concentration. That concentration is the dissociation constant, K D.
scenes.caption: Half fill at a very low concentration. That concentration is the dissociation constant, KD.
scenes.visual: The curve's midpoint is marked. On screen: KD = 0.08 nM, half the sites filled. Small label: free paroxetine, wild-type human SERT in HEK293 cell membranes.
scenes.narration: Half fill at a very low concentration. That concentration is the dissociation constant, KD.

scenes.tts: Nine in ten takes nine times that concentration.
scenes.visual: A marker climbs the curve to 90%. On screen: 90% at 0.72 nM, 9 × KD.
scenes.narration: Nine in ten takes nine times that concentration.

scenes.tts: Ninety nine in a hundred takes eleven times the ninety percent concentration.
scenes.caption: Ninety-nine in a hundred takes eleven times the 90% concentration.
scenes.visual: The marker crawls on to 99% along the flat top. On screen: 99% at 7.92 nM, 11 × the 90% concentration.
scenes.narration: Ninety-nine in a hundred takes eleven times the 90% concentration.

scenes.tts: The curve flattens at the top, so the last few sites cost far more drug.
scenes.visual: The flat top of the curve glows. Label: the last few percent cost the most.
scenes.narration: The curve flattens at the top, so the last few sites cost far more drug.

scenes.tts: Do those last few sites matter? Build a simple model to find out.
scenes.visual: The remaining 10 empty dots pulse. A model card: transporter is the only way out; far below saturation; occupancy held fixed; one-site equilibrium binding; block follows the binding KD.
scenes.narration: Do those last few sites matter? Build a simple model to find out.

scenes.tts: Suppose the transporter is the only way out, and is far from busy. Block half, and serotonin lingers twice as long.
scenes.visual: The model card shrinks to a corner. Below, a trace of serotonin against time after one release. A control decay, then a second decay twice as long. Label: half blocked, two times.
scenes.narration: Suppose the transporter is the only way out, and is far from busy. Block half, and serotonin lingers twice as long.

scenes.tts: Block nine in ten, and it lingers ten times as long.
scenes.visual: A third decay, ten times as long. Label: nine in ten blocked, ten times.
scenes.narration: Block nine in ten, and it lingers ten times as long.

scenes.tts: Block ninety nine in a hundred, and it lingers about a hundred times as long.
scenes.caption: Block ninety-nine in a hundred, and it lingers about a hundred times as long.
scenes.visual: A fourth decay stretches off the right edge. Label: ninety-nine in a hundred blocked, about a hundred times.
scenes.narration: Block ninety-nine in a hundred, and it lingers about a hundred times as long.

scenes.tts: That stretch is the factor one plus L over K. L is the free drug concentration. K is the drug's half fill concentration.
scenes.caption: That stretch is the factor 1 + L/K. L is the free drug concentration. K is the drug's half-fill concentration.
scenes.visual: On screen only: f = L / (K + L), and stretch = 1 / (1 − f) = 1 + L/K.
scenes.narration: That stretch is the factor 1 + L/K. L is the free drug concentration. K is the drug's half-fill concentration.

scenes.tts: Real tissue has other routes out. They make all three numbers smaller, and limit the stretch most when the block is nearly complete.
scenes.visual: The serotonin decays stay smooth exponentials, none clipped. Beside them, a separate small plot of decay-time stretch against share blocked, labelled illustrative: other routes out, fixed and first-order, 5% of baseline clearance. Points at 50%, 90% and 99% blocked read 1.9, 6.9 and 16.8 times, against 2, 10 and 100 with no other route; a dashed horizontal asymptote at 20 on this stretch plot. Label: other routes limit the stretch, most near full block.
scenes.narration: Real tissue has other routes out. They make all three numbers smaller, and limit the stretch most when the block is nearly complete.

scenes.tts: The same factor appears at a receptor. Picture gabba's dose response curve.
scenes.caption: The same factor appears at a receptor. Picture GABA's dose-response curve.
scenes.visual: A new graph: GABA concentration on a log axis, current up the side. A control S-shaped curve rises to a maximum.
scenes.narration: The same factor appears at a receptor. Picture GABA's dose-response curve.

scenes.tts: A competitive antagonist slides the curve right. You need more gabba, by that same factor, but you still reach the top.
scenes.caption: A competitive antagonist slides the curve right. You need more GABA, by that same factor, but you still reach the top.
scenes.visual: A bicuculline curve slides right in parallel and rises to the same maximum. Arrow between midpoints labelled 1 + [B]/KB.
scenes.narration: A competitive antagonist slides the curve right. You need more GABA, by that same factor, but you still reach the top.

scenes.tts: Diazepam, a modulator at a separate site, slides the curve to the left instead.
scenes.visual: A diazepam curve slides left of the control.
scenes.narration: Diazepam, a modulator at a separate site, slides the curve to the left instead.

scenes.tts: Keep adding bicuculline. Then, separately, keep adding diazepam. What happens to each curve?
scenes.visual: Two sliders, one for each drug, poised at the left. On screen: What happens to each curve? A five-second countdown ring.
scenes.narration: Keep adding bicuculline. Then, separately, keep adding diazepam. What happens to each curve?

scenes.tts: The antagonist keeps pushing the curve right, for as long as you add more.
scenes.visual: The bicuculline slider moves right; its curve keeps sliding right, top unchanged.
scenes.narration: The antagonist keeps pushing the curve right, for as long as you add more.

scenes.tts: The modulator stops. Once its own sites are full, it can do no more. That is its ceiling.
scenes.visual: The diazepam slider moves right; its curve slides left, then stops. Label: ceiling.
scenes.narration: The modulator stops. Once its own sites are full, it can do no more. That is its ceiling.

scenes.tts: One warning. This rule is for blockers that compete, not for agonists.
scenes.visual: A card: 1 + L/K is for competitive blockers.
scenes.narration: One warning. This rule is for blockers that compete, not for agonists.

scenes.tts: An agonist is different. With spare receptors, filling a tenth of them can give about half the full effect.
scenes.visual: A receptor field with one in ten filled beside a response bar at half height. Label: spare receptors.
scenes.narration: An agonist is different. With spare receptors, filling a tenth of them can give about half the full effect.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: if the transporter is the only way out, the last few percent blocked stretch the signal most.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: If the transporter is the only way out, the last few percent blocked stretch the signal most. Below, smaller: Next: a mechanism is not a cause.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: if the transporter is the only way out, the last few percent blocked stretch the signal most.
